topic: Same salary, different benefits: income-tested benefits (CGEB, CCB) use adjusted family net income — your line 23600 net income plus your spouse's or common-law partner's; and both partners must file a return to start or keep receiving them

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): CGEB July 2026–June 2027 (2025 base year). Nora, single, net income $45,000 ≤ $46,432 → $679. Sam, same $45,000, partner $35,000 → family net income $80,000; $80,000 − $46,432 = $33,568 over; × 5% = $1,678.40 > couple maximum $890 → $0. No children.

spoken.thr: forty-six thousand four hundred and thirty-two
spoken.over: thirty-three thousand five hundred and sixty-eight

sources.afni: canada.ca CRA (line 23600 / benefits): if you have a spouse or common-law partner, your adjusted net incomes are combined to get your adjusted family net income (AFNI); report your spouse's net income even if it is zero
sources.file: CRA Federal Income Tax and Benefit Information 2025 (5000-G): file a 2025 return if you or your spouse want to begin or continue receiving credits and benefits such as the CCB; if you have a spouse or common-law partner, they also have to file; CCB statistics page: recipients and their spouse are required to file to receive a CCB payment
sources.cgeb: canada.ca CRA CGEB how much (July 2026–June 2027): $679 single, $890 couple; phase-out above $46,432 at 5% (Budget 2026)
